question: Should OpenClaw sponsor an experiment-gated core Doctor surface for Claw lifecycle ownership and drift diagnostics once the prerequisite ownership stack is accepted?
rationale: The PR adds a new core lifecycle capability while VISION.md prefers a lean core and plugin-first optional functionality; the environment gate does not establish long-term ownership, support, or stack-landing policy.

options.title: Sponsor the core diagnostics surface
options.body: Accept the experiment-gated core direction after the prerequisite ownership contract and current-head real behavior proof are complete.

options.title: Defer the diagnostics slice with the RFC stack
options.body: Keep this PR open but unlanded until maintainers evaluate the prerequisite and dependent Claws lifecycle slices together.

options.title: Decline the core lifecycle direction
options.body: Close the implementation stack if maintainers do not want lifecycle ownership and reconciliation to become a core capability.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core diagnostics surface
recommendation.body: Accept the experiment-gated core direction after the prerequisite ownership contract and current-head real behavior proof are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-state and Doctor architecture work most directly connects this owner to the persistent-state contract and the core-boundary choice.
